passages.text: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not resort to sorcery as on previous occasions, but he turned his face toward the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from outside Israel.
Balaam saw that the LORD was pleased to bless Israel.
Balaam understood that God wanted to bless Israel.
Balaam did not use sorcery this time.
Balaam had used sorcery before.
Balaam turned his face toward the wilderness.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא בִּלְעָ֗ם כִּ֣י ט֞וֹב בְּעֵינֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹא־ הָלַ֥ךְ כְּפַֽעַם־ בְּפַ֖עַם לִקְרַ֣את נְחָשִׁ֑ים וַיָּ֥שֶׁת אֶל־ הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר פָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: When Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came upon him, and he lifted up an oracle, saying: “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open: How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from outside Israel.
Balaam looked up.
He saw Israel.
Israel was camped by their tribes.
The Spirit of God came upon Balaam.
Balaam spoke a prophecy.
He said, “This is the prophecy of Balaam, son of Beor.
This is the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open.
This is the prophecy of one who hears the words of God.
This is the prophecy of one who sees a vision from the Almighty.
He bows down with eyes wide open.
He said, ‘How lovely are your tents, Jacob.
How lovely are your dwellings, Israel.’”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א בִלְעָ֜ם אֶת־ עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֹׁכֵ֖ן לִשְׁבָטָ֑יו וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִֽים׃ וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נְאֻ֤ם בִּלְעָם֙ בְּנ֣וֹ בְעֹ֔ר וּנְאֻ֥ם הַגֶּ֖בֶר שְׁתֻ֥ם הָעָֽיִן׃ נְאֻ֕ם שֹׁמֵ֖עַ אִמְרֵי־ אֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַחֲזֵ֤ה שַׁדַּי֙ יֶֽחֱזֶ֔ה נֹפֵ֖ל וּגְל֥וּי עֵינָֽיִם׃ מַה־ טֹּ֥בוּ אֹהָלֶ֖יךָ יַעֲקֹ֑ב מִשְׁכְּנֹתֶ֖יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: They spread out like palm groves, like gardens beside a stream, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
passages.sermon:
Israel is the subject.
Israel is encamped tribe by tribe.
The Spirit of God comes upon Balaam.
Balaam sees Israel.
Israel spreads out.
Israel spreads out like palm groves.
Israel spreads out like gardens beside a stream.
The LORD plants Israel like aloes.
Israel stands like cedars beside the waters.
passages.original: כִּנְחָלִ֣ים נִטָּ֔יוּ כְּגַנֹּ֖ת עֲלֵ֣י נָהָ֑ר כַּאֲהָלִים֙ נָטַ֣ע יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲרָזִ֖ים עֲלֵי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will have abundant water. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
passages.sermon:
Balaam spoke a prophecy from God.
He said Israel will have great blessing.
Water will pour from his buckets.
His descendants will have plenty of water.
Israel’s king will be greater than Agag.
Israel’s kingdom will be lifted up.
passages.original: יִֽזַּל־ מַ֙יִם֙ מִדָּ֣לְיָ֔ו וְזַרְע֖וֹ בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְיָרֹ֤ם מֵֽאֲגַג֙ מַלְכּ֔וֹ וְתִנַּשֵּׂ֖א מַלְכֻתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: God brought him out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox, to devour hostile nations and crush their bones, to pierce them with arrows.
passages.sermon:
God brought Israel out of Egypt.
God gave Israel great strength.
Israel’s strength was like a wild ox.
Israel will defeat hostile nations.
Israel will crush the bones of its enemies.
Israel will pierce its enemies with arrows.
passages.original: אֵ֚ל מוֹצִיא֣וֹ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם כְּתוֹעֲפֹ֥ת רְאֵ֖ם ל֑וֹ יֹאכַ֞ל גּוֹיִ֣ם צָרָ֗יו וְעַצְמֹתֵיהֶ֛ם יְגָרֵ֖ם וְחִצָּ֥יו יִמְחָֽץ׃

passages.text: He crouches, he lies down like a lion; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you.”
passages.sermon:
Israel is strong and fearless like a lion.
Israel crouches down and lies like a lion.
Israel also lies like a lioness.
No one dares to wake him.
God blesses everyone who blesses Israel.
God curses everyone who curses Israel.
passages.original: כָּרַ֨ע שָׁכַ֧ב כַּאֲרִ֛י וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֣י יְקִימֶ֑נּוּ מְבָרֲכֶ֣יךָ בָר֔וּךְ וְאֹרְרֶ֖יךָ אָרֽוּר׃

passages.text: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together and said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times.
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak became very angry with Balaam.
Balak struck his hands together.
Balak spoke to Balaam.
Balak said, “I called you to curse my enemies.
But you have blessed them instead.
You have blessed them three times.”
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֤ף בָּלָק֙ אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיִּסְפֹּ֖ק אֶת־ כַּפָּ֑יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בָּלָ֜ק אֶל־ בִּלְעָ֗ם לָקֹ֤ב אֹֽיְבַי֙ קְרָאתִ֔יךָ וְהִנֵּה֙ בֵּרַ֣כְתָּ בָרֵ֔ךְ זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִֽים׃

passages.text: Therefore, flee at once to your home! I said I would richly reward you, but instead the LORD has denied your reward.”
passages.sermon:
Balak was the king of Moab.
\r\nBalak spoke to Balaam.
\r\nBalak told Balaam to leave immediately.
\r\nBalak said, "Go back to your home."
\r\nBalak said he had planned to honor Balaam with a great reward.
\r\nBalak said the LORD had kept Balaam from receiving this honor.
\r\nBalak did not give Balaam the reward.
\r\nThe LORD prevented Balaam from being honored by Balak.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה בְּרַח־ לְךָ֣ אֶל־ מְקוֹמֶ֑ךָ אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ כַּבֵּ֣ד אֲכַבֶּדְךָ֔ וְהִנֵּ֛ה מְנָעֲךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה מִכָּבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not already tell the messengers you sent me that even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything of my own accord, good or bad, to go beyond the command of the LORD? I will speak whatever the LORD says.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balak was a king who wanted Balaam to curse Israel.
Balaam spoke to Balak.
Balaam said, “I already told your messengers this message.
You sent them to me.
Even if you, Balak, gave me your whole house filled with silver and gold, I could not do anything on my own.
I cannot do good or bad by my own decision.
I cannot go beyond the command of the LORD.
I will only speak what the LORD tells me to say.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר בִּלְעָ֖ם אֶל־ בָּלָ֑ק הֲלֹ֗א גַּ֧ם אֶל־ מַלְאָכֶ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁלַ֥חְתָּ אֵלַ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי לֵאמֹֽר׃ אִם־ יִתֶּן־ לִ֨י בָלָ֜ק מְלֹ֣א בֵיתוֹ֮ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָב֒ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֗ל לַעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־ פִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת טוֹבָ֛ה א֥וֹ רָעָ֖ה מִלִּבִּ֑י אֲשֶׁר־ יְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam is a prophet who speaks for God.
Balaam spoke to Balak, the king of Moab.
Balaam said, “Now I am going back to my people.
Come here.
I will give you advice.
I will tell you what this people, Israel, will do to your people in the future.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנְנִ֥י הוֹלֵ֖ךְ לְעַמִּ֑י לְכָה֙ אִיעָ֣צְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֛ה לְעַמְּךָ֖ בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying, “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel. He will crush the skulls of Moab and strike down all the sons of Sheth.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balaam was the son of Beor.
Balaam spoke a prophecy.
Balaam was a man whose eyes were open.
Balaam heard the words of God.
Balaam had knowledge from the Most High.
Balaam saw a vision from the Almighty.
Balaam bowed down with his eyes wide open.
Balaam said, “I see him, but not now.”
Balaam said, “I behold him, but he is not near.”
A star will come forth from Jacob.
A scepter will arise from Israel.
He will crush the skulls of Moab.
He will strike down all the sons of Sheth.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נְאֻ֤ם בִּלְעָם֙ בְּנ֣וֹ בְעֹ֔ר וּנְאֻ֥ם הַגֶּ֖בֶר שְׁתֻ֥ם הָעָֽיִן׃ נְאֻ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ אִמְרֵי־ אֵ֔ל וְיֹדֵ֖עַ דַּ֣עַת עֶלְי֑וֹן מַחֲזֵ֤ה שַׁדַּי֙ יֶֽחֱזֶ֔ה נֹפֵ֖ל וּגְל֥וּי עֵינָֽיִם׃ אֶרְאֶ֙נּוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א עַתָּ֔ה אֲשׁוּרֶ֖נּוּ וְלֹ֣א קָר֑וֹב דָּרַ֨ךְ כּוֹכָ֜ב מִֽיַּעֲקֹ֗ב וְקָ֥ם שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמָחַץ֙ פַּאֲתֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב וְקַרְקַ֖ר כָּל־ בְּנֵי־ שֵׁ֔ת׃

passages.text: Edom will become a possession, as will Seir, his enemy; but Israel will perform with valor.
passages.sermon: Edom will become a possession.\r\nSeir, Edom’s enemy, will also become a possession.\r\nIsrael will act with strength and bravery.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה אֱד֜וֹם יְרֵשָׁ֗ה וְהָיָ֧ה יְרֵשָׁ֛ה שֵׂעִ֖יר אֹיְבָ֑יו וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹ֥שֶׂה חָֽיִל׃

passages.text: A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city.”
passages.sermon: A ruler will come from Jacob.\r\nThis ruler will destroy the survivors of the city.

passages.text: Then Balaam saw Amalek and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Amalek was first among the nations, but his end is destruction.”
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
Balaam saw Amalek.
Balaam spoke a message from God.
Balaam said, “Amalek was the first among the nations.
But Amalek’s end is destruction.”
passages.original: וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר רֵאשִׁ֤ית גּוֹיִם֙ עֲמָלֵ֔ק וְאַחֲרִית֖וֹ עֲדֵ֥י אֹבֵֽד׃

passages.text: Next he saw the Kenites and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.
passages.sermon:
Balaam saw the Kenites.
Balaam spoke a message about them.
He said, “Your home is strong.
You live in safety.
You have built your nest high in the rocks.”
passages.original: וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־ הַקֵּינִ֔י וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֵיתָן֙ מֽוֹשָׁבֶ֔ךָ וְשִׂ֥ים בַּסֶּ֖לַע קִנֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Yet Kain will be destroyed when Asshur takes you captive.”
passages.sermon:
Kain is a group of people called the Kenites.
Asshur is a nation that will come against them.
Asshur will take the Kenites captive.
Kain will be destroyed when this happens.
passages.original: כִּ֥י אִם־ יִהְיֶ֖ה לְבָ֣עֵֽר קָ֑יִן עַד־ מָ֖ה אַשּׁ֥וּר תִּשְׁבֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Once more Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?
passages.sermon: Balaam was a prophet.\r\nBalaam spoke another message.\r\nBalaam said, “Who can live unless God allows it?”
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א מְשָׁל֖וֹ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר א֕וֹי מִ֥י יִחְיֶ֖ה מִשֻּׂמ֥וֹ אֵֽל׃

passages.text: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will perish forever.”
passages.sermon:
Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus.
These ships will subdue Asshur.
They will also subdue Eber.
But these ships will perish forever.
passages.original: וְצִים֙ מִיַּ֣ד כִּתִּ֔ים וְעִנּ֥וּ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְעִנּוּ־ עֵ֑בֶר וְגַם־ ה֖וּא עֲדֵ֥י אֹבֵֽד׃

passages.text: Then Balaam arose and returned to his homeland, and Balak also went on his way.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet from outside Israel.
Balaam stood up.
Balaam left.
Balaam returned to his own land.
Balak was the king of Moab.
Balak also left.
Balak went on his own way.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ וַיָּ֣שָׁב לִמְקֹמ֑וֹ וְגַם־ בָּלָ֖ק הָלַ֥ךְ לְדַרְכּֽוֹ׃פ
